title: Laxative treatment perturbs gut microbiome composition and metabolism in humans independent of short-term fiber consumption: a randomized controlled crossover intervention study.
abstract: Gastrointestinal transit time is a major ecological determinant of the human gut microbiome, yet causal evidence that disentangles the effects of diet from those of the gut environment remains limited. Here, we conducted a randomized, controlled crossover trial in healthy adults (nine females, four males) consuming fully standardized high-fiber (40 g/d) or low-fiber (10 g/d) diets to assess how manipulating the gut environment using an osmotic laxative (Movicol) affects gut microbial composition

title: Microbiota-Bile acid decoupling contributes to altered postnatal growth and metabolism in sFGR: a twin-paired dynamic study with FMT validation.
abstract: Selective fetal growth restriction (sFGR) increases the risk of adverse long-term metabolic outcomes, yet the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. Bile acids (BAs) mediate gut microbiota-host metabolic crosstalk, and their early-life perturbation may underlie sFGR-associated health risks. Using a monochorionic diamniotic twin cohort (25 concordant pairs, 22 sFGR pairs), we developed a twin-specific analytical framework integrating birth weight deviation, intra-pair difference, and time-weighted

title: Modulation of neuroimmunity by early-life microbiota colonization.
abstract: Early life (fetal period to 2-3 y postnatally) is a critical window for the coordinated development of the intestine, lungs, and brain. As core pathways mediating microbe-immune-neuron crosstalk, the gut-brain and lung-brain axes drive cross-organ communication via early-life microbiota colonization, profoundly shaping immune maturation and neurodevelopmental trajectories. During fetal development, maternal microbial metabolites cross the placenta to prime in utero immune and neural development.

title: Gut Holdemania filiformis raises brain isoallopregnanolone in progesterone-treated female mice.
abstract: Neuroactive 5α-steroids modulate γ-aminobutyric acid type A (GABAA) receptor signaling and are of growing therapeutic interest: allopregnanolone (3α,5α) is a positive allosteric modulator, whereas its 3β-epimer isoallopregnanolone antagonizes this action and is itself in clinical development. Their formation has been attributed to host enzymes in the liver, gastrointestinal tract, and central nervous system, whereas a contribution from any individual gut bacterium has not been demonstrated. title: Gut microbiome patterns in a multi-ethnic Asian population within a shared urban environment.
abstract: The gut microbiome composition varies across human populations, but its characteristics and determinants in a multi-ethnic setting remain incompletely understood. Singapore, a multicultural city-state, provides a context in which culturally diverse groups share a broadly similar built environment. Using the Health for Life in Singapore (HELIOS) cohort, we profiled the gut microbiome of ethnic Chinese, Indian, and Malay participants (n = 861) residing in the country. These ethnicity-diet-microbio

title: Acetate-FFAR2 signaling induces neutrophil-derived IL-22 to protect against colitis.
abstract: Short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs) produced by gut microbiota are key modulators of intestinal homeostasis and immune responses. Although their anti-inflammatory roles are well established, the mechanisms by which SCFAs-FFAR2 shapes neutrophil function and influences intestinal inflammation remain unclear. Here, we demonstrate that dietary fiber or acetate protect mice from DSS-induced colitis despite increasing neutrophil infiltration into the intestinal tissue. Importantly, neutrophils are requir
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America

title: Role of Bile Acids in Colorectal Diseases.
abstract: Bile acids (BAs) have functions well beyond fat digestion. They also serve as signals linking the gut microbiota to gut health. This review examines how BAs affect colorectal diseases and how this knowledge can guide diagnosis and treatment.

title: High-throughput screening of patient iPSC-derived neurons identifies the gut microbial metabolites that attenuate Alzheimer's disease pathology.
abstract: Gut microbiota-derived metabolites influence the gut-brain axis and may impact Alzheimer's disease (AD) pathology. However, the microbial metabolites involved in this process and their functional roles are largely unknown. We screened 352 gut metabolites in induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSC)-derived neurons from individuals with AD to identify compounds that reduce tau hyperphosphorylation. title: Formation of an inulin biocorona on food-grade titanium dioxide nanoparticles alleviates gut microbiota dysbiosis and inflammatory responses under calorie restriction.
abstract: Food-grade nanoparticles undergo dynamic interactions with dietary biomolecules during gastrointestinal transit, leading to the formation of a biomolecular corona that determines their biological identity and health effects. Here, we investigated whether an inulin-derived biocorona could modulate the gastrointestinal fate and biological responses of the nanoscale fraction of titanium dioxide (TiO2) under normal and calorie-restricted conditions. In mice fed a normal diet, oral exposure to TiO2 n

title: A NanAKE-like pathway enables sialic acid catabolism in gut microbiome member Hungatella hathewayi.
abstract: Sialic acids are abundant components of host- and diet-derived glycans in the human gut that shape microbial fitness and interspecies competition. Free sialic acids can be a nutrient source but also stimulate inflammation and pathogen colonization. Escherichia coli and Bacteroides spp. catabolize sialic acids via the NanAKE and NanLE-RokA pathways, yet the metabolic capacity of many microbiome members remains undefined. To identify sialic acid-catabolizing bacteria, we cultured fecal samples fro

title: Diet correction after perinatal deficiency in vitamin B9 and B12 fails to rescue gut dysbiosis, serotonin pathway and psychiatric-like behavior in adult rats.
abstract: Perinatal dietary deficiencies such as vitamin B9 and B12 induce persistent gut dysbiosis, metabolic, physiologic imbalances and behavioral defects that could extend into adulthood, but the underlying fetal programming mechanisms remain poorly understood. We have investigated the long-term consequences of a perinatal vitamin B9 and B12 deficiency associated dysbiosis and focusing on sex-dependent outcomes related to behavior and molecular markers of the gut-brain axis. Despite post-weaning diet

title: Primary sclerosing cholangitis: epidemiology, risk factors, pathophysiology, clinical features, diagnosis, and management.
abstract: Primary sclerosing cholangitis (PSC) is a rare cholangiopathy characterized by multifocal inflammation and fibrostenotic remodeling of the bile ducts, cholestasis, and increased risks of cholangiocarcinoma and colorectal cancer. No pharmacological therapy has yet improved transplant-free survival. Clinical care therefore depends on accurate phenotyping, surveillance, treatment of biliary and intestinal complications, and timely liver transplantation. title: BGN4-derived intestinal metabolite 6-hydroxynicotinic acid alleviates hepatocytes ferroptosis in MAFLD via Nrf2/SREBP1/CYP2E1 axis.
abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated fatty liver disease (MAFLD) is closely associated with dysbiosis of the gut microbiota. In this study, we investigated the biological effects and underlying mechanisms of Bifidobacterium bifidum BGN4 and its intestinal metabolite, 6-hydroxynicotinic acid (6-HNA), in regulating hepatocyte ferroptosis in MAFLD.
journal: Daru : journal of Faculty of Pharmacy, Tehran University of Medical Sciences

title: Lactobacillus plantarum CCFM639 attenuates high-salt-induced hypertension involving IL-17A signaling suppression.
abstract: Chronic high-salt (HS) intake induces hypertension and is associated with reduced intestinal Lactobacillus. This study investigated underlying mechanisms for Lactobacillus plantarum CCFM639 (CCFM639) alleviating HS-induced hypertension.

title: Gut microbiota-driven imbalance of the gut-brain-immune homeostatic network in constipation: Pathogenic mechanisms and evolving therapeutic prospects.
abstract: Chronic constipation (CC) is increasingly recognized as a systems-level disorder that cannot be explained by impaired intestinal motility alone. Here, we integrate evidence from clinical cohorts, animal models, and mechanistic studies to examine how gut microbial dysbiosis and altered microbial metabolites perturb epithelial barrier integrity, immune homeostasis, enteric neural activity, and gut-brain signaling. We propose a "gut-brain-immune homeostatic network" in which short-chain fatty acids

title: Isolation, identification and prebiotic potential of polysaccharides from fresh goji berry.
abstract: Polysaccharides from fresh goji berry were isolated and characterized to investigate their structures, simulated gastrointestinal digestion, and lactic acid bacteria (LAB) growth-supporting effects. Hot-water extraction, 50% ethanol precipitation, and chromatographic separation yielded two acidic polysaccharides, LBP1 and LBP2, with apparent molecular weights of 13.47 ± 0.24 and 185.0 ± 3.0 kDa, respectively. title: Ovarian function via gut microbiota-driven serotonin dysregulation in zebrafish.
abstract: Ciprofloxacin (CIP) is frequently detected in aquatic environments, yet its effects on reproduction through gut microbiota-mediated pathways remain unclear. Adult female zebrafish were exposed to 5,000 ng/L CIP for 30 days and evaluated using histology, hormone assays, metagenomics, metabolomics, transcriptomics, and fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT). CIP impaired folliculogenesis, reduced follicle-stimulating hormone, luteinizing hormone, and estradiol levels, and disrupted intestinal barr

title: Oral live and heat-killed Ligilactobacillus salivarius Ls.0403 alleviate MC903-induced atopic dermatitis-like inflammation and are associated with gut microbiota changes in mice.
abstract: Atopic dermatitis (AD) is a chronic, relapsing inflammatory skin disease that often requires long-term management. Probiotics have been investigated as adjunctive approaches for AD, but their effects are highly strain specific. Among these, Ligilactobacillus salivarius has shown potential in previous AD studies, yet the effects of different strains remain insufficiently characterized. In this study, we screened 19 human-derived L. salivarius isolates and selected Ls.0403, which exhibited favorab

title: Microbiome-dependent phytosterol sulfates production and tissue distribution in mice.
abstract: Microbial biotransformation of dietary lipids, such as cholesterol, influences host homeostasis. Despite extensive studies on animal sterols in host-microbiota interactions, the role of phytosterols in homeostasis remains unclear. In this study, we characterized phytosterol sulfates as microbiota-derived metabolites using untargeted lipidomic data mining. The levels of sitosterol sulfate (SIS), campesterol sulfate, and stigmasterol sulfate, the three major phytosterol sulfates, along with copros

title: Gut microbiota composition of India's Baiga tribe: Insights from an indigenous particularly vulnerable tribal group.
abstract: The transition from traditional foraging lifestyles to modernized urban environments is associated with reduced human gut microbiome diversity. To examine this shift within the Indian subcontinent, we used shotgun metagenomics to compare the gut microbiota of 50 adults: 25 from the indigenous, foraging, and particularly vulnerable Baiga tribe and 25 from an urban population in Bhopal, Central India. The Baiga maintained a diverse ecosystem enriched with fiber-degrading bacteria such as Roseburia

title: EndD mediates butyrate-dependent toxin release and sporulation in Clostridioides difficile.
abstract: Clostridioides difficile is an urgent threat to human health. Current treatments for C. difficile infections (CDIs) are antibiotics and microbiome restoration therapy (MRT) for recurrent cases. However, antibiotics contribute to antibiotic resistance and recurrent CDIs, and the long-term sustainability and accessibility of MRTs remain to be determined. title: An HA-Coated Akkermansia-Paeoniflorin Biohybrid Enables Sustained Oral Delivery for Gut-Gonad Axis Protection.
abstract: Living biohybrid materials offer a unique opportunity to couple oral drug delivery with host-microbiome interactions, yet maintaining carrier integrity, cargo retention, and biological function under gastrointestinal constraints remains challenging. Here, we engineered a hyaluronic acid (HA)-coated Akkermansia muciniphila-paeoniflorin biohybrid (PF@AKK@HA) through vacuum-enabled paeoniflorin loading followed by HA shell stabilization. Structural and colloidal analyses confirmed preserved bacteri

title: Distinct Probiotic Effects of Limosilactobacillus fermentum Perfectus001 and Bifidobacterium animalis subsp. lactis Perfectus006 in a Rat Model of Spleen qi Deficiency Syndrome.
abstract: Spleen qi deficiency syndrome (SDS) is characterized by chronic fatigue, gastrointestinal dysfunction, and systemic metabolic disturbances and has been associated with gut microbial dysbiosis and chronic inflammation. This study evaluated the effects of two probiotic strains, Limosilactobacillus fermentum Perfectus001 (LFP) and Bifidobacterium animalis subsp. lactis Perfectus006 (BAP), in an SDS rat model. Both probiotic strains significantly ameliorated SDS-like phenotypes, including reduced bl

title: The role of the gut microbiome in stress responses of dogs: gut-brain axis and microbiome-targeted interventions.
abstract: Stress poses a significant threat to canine welfare and adoptability, particularly in animal shelters where dogs are exposed to multiple environmental and social stressors. Growing evidence suggests that the gut-brain axis (GBA), a bidirectional communication network linking the gastrointestinal tract and the central nervous system, plays a critical role in regulating stress responses. This review summarizes the mechanisms through which the gut microbiome influences canine behavior and physiolog
journal: The Journal of veterinary medical science

title: Antibiotic heteroresistance observed across commensal Lactobacillus species.
abstract: Lactobacilli are prevalent members of the microbiota in the intestinal and reproductive tracts of humans and other species. They are commonly used in probiotics due to their beneficial effects on human health, including their association with protection from numerous chronic diseases. In addition, these microbes are often prescribed to maintain their presence in the host during antibiotic therapy, as well as to treat diarrhea caused by antibiotics. Despite many studies examining the beneficial e

title: Early-Life Overfeeding Drives Lasting Species-Level Shifts of the Gut Microbiome and Exacerbates Allergic Asthma in Mice.
abstract: Early-life overweight is associated with increased asthma risk in children, but the mechanisms linking metabolic status, the gut microbiome and airway disease remain poorly explored. To address this, we used a litter-size reduction model in mice to examine how early-life overfeeding and overweight shape gut microbial development and later allergic asthma severity. Overfed offspring displayed increased body weight, adiposity and altered body proportions from early postnatal life onward, with more

title: Population-scale identification of gut commensals that antagonize antibiotic-resistant pathogens.
abstract: Antimicrobial resistance poses a global threat, yet microbiome-encoded defenses against antibiotic resistance gene (ARG)-associated pathogens remain poorly defined. Here, we analyze 12,238 human gut metagenomes and prioritize 159 commensal species ("coexcluders") that show inverse associations with ARG-associated pathogenic taxa. title: Synergistic Anti-Tumour Strategy Combining Valerate, Butyrate, Neurotensin Pathway Modulation from Gut Microbiota, and Non-Typhoidal Salmonella in Hepatocellular Carcinoma.
abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remains a major cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide, with disease progression and treatment outcomes influenced by tumour heterogeneity, therapeutic resistance, and an immunosuppressive tumour microenvironment. Increasing evidence highlights the gut-liver axis as an important regulator of hepatic inflammation, metabolic homeostasis, and tumour-associated immune responses. title: Human Milk-Derived Synbiotics Attenuate DSS-Induced Colitis in Mice via Promoting Intestinal Colonization of Lachnospira.
abstract: 2'-Fucosyllactose (2'-FL) exhibits prebiotic properties, but its ability to enhance probiotic efficacy in ulcerative colitis (UC) is incompletely understood. Here, we show that 2'-FL effectively enhances the protective effect of Bifidobacterium bifidum B-67 against DSS-induced colitis in mice. Combination therapy outperformed individual treatments, suppressing pro-inflammatory cytokines and restoring mucosal integrity. journal: Journal of agricultural and food chemistry

title: Food-Grade Kappa-Carrageenan Induces Liver Injury through the FXR/FGF15 Pathway in Mice.
abstract: Food-grade carrageenan (CGN) is widely used as a food additive, but its potential health risks remain controversial. This study investigated the effects of dietary food-grade kappa-CGN (κ-CGN) on liver health in mice. Our findings demonstrated that dietary κ-CGN induced liver inflammation, oxidative stress, and fibrosis. Metabolomic analyses identified elevated circulatory bile acids as a potential contributor to κ-CGN-induced liver injury. 16S rRNA sequencing revealed gut microbiota dysbiosis a
journal: Journal of agricultural and food chemistry

title: The impact of childhood obesity on the developing skeleton.
abstract: Childhood obesity is an increasingly prevalent global health concern associated with significant metabolic, endocrine, and skeletal consequences. During critical periods of growth and peak bone mineralisation, excessive adiposity may impair skeletal development by disrupting bone formation and remodeling. title: Forsythiaside A enhances host defense against Pseudomonas aeruginosa pneumonia by modulating gut microbiota-derived indole-3-lactic acid and AhR signaling.
abstract: Pseudomonas aeruginosa pneumonia poses a major clinical challenge due to its high pathogenicity and rising antibiotic resistance. Forsythiae Fructus has long been used in traditional Chinese medicine for treating lung diseases, particularly bacterial pneumonia. However, whether its major bioactive constituent, forsythiaside A (FA), exerts therapeutic effects against P. aeruginosa-induced pneumonia and the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. title: Alcohol-Tolerant Lactiplantibacillus plantarum LBP-L01 Prevents Acute Alcoholic Liver Injury by Reducing Blood Alcohol Concentration and Modulating Gut Microbiota in Mice.
abstract: Alcoholic liver disease (ALD) is a major global health concern with limited effective interventions. This study screened and identified a lactic acid bacterial strain with potent ethanol-degrading capacity, designated as Lactiplantibacillus plantarum LBP-L01. Sequence alignment-based annotation of the L. plantarum LBP-L01 genome identified genes involved in alcohol metabolism. title: Time-restricted feeding prevents acute liver injury by suppressing microbial anabolism of uric acid.
abstract: Time-restricted feeding (TRF) is known to improve metabolic and physiological rhythms; however, its role in acute liver injury (ALI) is unknown. Herein, we demonstrate that TRF ameliorates ALI through the gut microbiota across multiple murine models, particularly the acetaminophen-induced ALI. Specifically, TRF reduces host-derived 3-methylhistamine to decrease Prevotella intermedia (P. intermedia), which expresses adenosine deaminase (ADA) to generate uric acid (UA) in the gut. title: Genome-resolved multi-omics characterizes bacterial, viral, and metabolic components associated with Parkinson's disease gut ecosystem variation.
abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) is increasingly recognized as a disorder involving the gut-brain axis, yet genome-resolved characterization of bacterial and viral communities with metabolic context remains limited. Here, we performed deep shotgun metagenomic sequencing and fecal metabolomic profiling in a high-altitude cohort comprising patients with PD and environmentally matched spouse controls (living at approximately 1,900 m altitude). We reconstructed 455 species-level genome bins (SGBs) and 2,957

title: Conformational and Rheological Changes of Hericium erinaceus Polysaccharides Driven by Molecular Weight Reduction and Their Impact on Prebiotic Effects.
abstract: Hericium erinaceus polysaccharide was degraded using microwave-assisted enzymatic hydrolysis to obtain four gradient molecular weight fractions (HePs). This study investigated the effects of molecular weight on their structural, rheological, and prebiotic properties. journal: Journal of agricultural and food chemistry

title: Polysaccharide from Ziyang black tea prevents high-fat diet-induced obesity by remodeling gut microbiota and promoting adipose thermogenesis.
abstract: This study aims to explore the mechanism of obesity prevention by polysaccharide extracted from Ziyang black tea (BTP). BTP is an acidic heteropolysaccharide, mainly composed of galactose (36.5%), arabinose (31.7%), and glucose (15.9%). Treating high-fat diet (HFD)-fed mice with BTP prevented weight gain, lowered adiposity and reduced liver steatosis. title: Podophyllotoxin-induced mammary gland injury via the gut-mammary gland axis mediated by gut microbiota-derived metabolite PAG and aberrant EGFR signaling in SD rats based on the toxicological evidence chain (TEC) concept.
abstract: Podophyllotoxin is a lignan isolated from Dysosma versipellis with well-established antitumor activity. In this study, we applied an upgraded toxicological evidence chain 2.0 framework to characterize podophyllotoxin-induced mammary toxicity in female rats and to probe the distal regulatory mechanism operating through the gut-mammary axis. Repeated oral exposure provoked acute toxic signs in the animals, and histomorphometric analysis revealed a significant loss of collagen fibers in mammary tis

title: Ligilactobacillus salivarius inhibits GII.4[P16] human norovirus replication in zebrafish larvae.
abstract: Human gut bacteria can modulate human norovirus (HuNoV) infection, underscoring the need to characterize virus-bacterium interactions. This study evaluated the effect of Ligilactobacillus salivarius on HuNoV GII.4[P16] replication using a zebrafish larva model. A GII.4[P16]-positive stool specimen was resuspended in phosphate-buffered saline (PBS), centrifuged, and the supernatant stored at -80°C. title: Commensal Bacteroides Strains Restrict Intestinal Colonization by Multidrug-Resistant Campylobacter jejuni.
abstract: Multidrug-resistant (MDR) Campylobacter jejuni is a foodborne pathogen that threatens public health and food safety. Intestinal colonization is a prerequisite for infection, yet protective commensal bacteria and the potential contributions of microbial metabolites remain poorly defined. This study integrates in vitro co-culture assays, epithelial cell models, mouse infection experiments, and multi-omics analyses to identify protective gut commensals and explore potential mechanisms. title: Species-specific bacteriophage-mediated engineering of an artificial microbiome composed of Bacteroides and Phocaeicola species.
abstract: Members of the genera Bacteroides and Phocaeicola have been involved in various health- and disease-related states, but their in situ functions have not been clearly elucidated yet. Targeted removal of specific bacterial species using bacteriophages is expected to facilitate in situ functional analysis of gut bacteria. title: Dietary butyric acid modulates physiological, gut microbiota and transcriptomic responses of Penaeus vannamei under low salinity conditions.
abstract: Low salinity culture is increasingly adopted in the farming of Penaeus vannamei; however, nutritional strategies that specifically target physiological resilience and their underlying mechanisms under low salinity conditions remain insufficiently understood. This study evaluated the effects of dietary butyric acid supplementation (0%, 1%, 2%, and 4%) on growth performance, physiological responses, gut microbiota composition, and hepatopancreas transcriptome of juvenile P. vannamei reared at a sa
journal: Comparative biochemistry and physiology. Part D, Genomics & proteomics

title: Analysis of metabolic interactions in an artificial consortium including butyrogenic gut microbes.
abstract: Cross-feeding interactions shape gut microbial communities and contribute to the establishment of bacteria associated with beneficial fermentation products such as butyrate. However, many gut microbes involved in fiber degradation and butyrate-associated trophic networks remain poorly characterized. title: Population-level characterisation of the human gut phageome and its association with microbial metabolites.
abstract: Bacteriophages, viruses infecting bacteria, are abundant in the human gut, but their population-level structure and metabolic associations remain unclear Here we present a foundational characterisation of the gut phageome using deep shotgun metagenomic data in a large population-based cohort (n = 1,069: TwinsUK). title: A metabolite-centered framework for microbiota-gut-brain communication linking constrained signaling to behavior and stress physiology.
abstract: The microbiota-gut-brain axis links gut microbial activity with host neurophysiology and behavior, but its mechanistic interpretation remains fragmented across individual metabolites, biological compartments, and experimental systems. title: Microbiota-gut-brain axis dysregulation in irritable bowel syndrome: mechanisms, clinical evidence, and therapeutic implications. a narrative review.
abstract: Irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) is a heterogeneous disorder of gut-brain interaction in which altered visceral sensitivity, motility, immune activity, epithelial permeability, and microbial metabolism may interact. Microbiota-related associations are frequently reported, but their direction and causal relevance remain uncertain. title: Metabolic disease engineers the colorectal cancer ecosystem.
abstract: Obesity and type 2 diabetes (T2D) increase colorectal cancer (CRC) risk, yet the mechanisms linking systemic metabolic dysfunction to carcinogenesis are usually considered independently. I propose that metabolic disease can act as an ecosystem engineer, altering the selective conditions in which neoplastic cells emerge and evolve. title: Ileal bile acid transporter inhibitors.
abstract: Pediatric cholestatic liver diseases, such as Alagille syndrome and progressive familial intrahepatic cholestasis, are rare genetic disorders characterized by impaired bile flow, systemic bile acid accumulation, and debilitating pruritus. Historically managed with supportive care or invasive surgical interventions, the therapeutic landscape has recently expanded with the introduction of ileal bile acid transporter (IBAT) inhibitors. journal: Journal of pediatric gastroenterology and nutrition

abstract: BackgroundMultiple pathophysiological mechanisms have been reported in animals with chronic enteropathy, as reflected by altered serum and fecal metabolites indicative of mucosal damage (e.g., fecal cholesterol, nervonic acid, arachidonic acid), malabsorption (e.g., serum cobalamin, fecal glucose), and loss of microbial function (e.g., fecal bile acid conversion). journal: Journal of feline medicine and surgery

title: Non-redundant cardiolipin synthase family proteins shape lipid composition and stress resilience in Bacteroides fragilis.
abstract: Gut-resident bacteria must withstand membrane-disrupting stresses, such as bile acids, to persist in the intestinal environment. The Bacteroidota are a dominant phylum of the human gut microbiota. However, the genes responsible for the synthesis of membrane lipids in this phylum remain relatively uncharacterized. title: Gut microbiota-associated metabolic alterations contribute to 6PPD-Q-induced intestinal barrier dysfunction in mice.
abstract: N-(1,3-Dimethylbutyl)-N'-phenyl-p-phenylenediamine quinone (6PPD-Q), a ubiquitous tire-derived contaminant detected in environmental matrices and human samples, poses potential intestinal health risks to mammals. However, the underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood. title: Incretin-Based Therapies and the Gut-Brain Axis in Neurodegenerative Diseases.
abstract: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs), originally developed for metabolic disorders, remain under active investigation as potential therapeutic candidates for neurodegenerative diseases, including Alzheimer's and Parkinson's disease, with clinical trials to date reporting both positive and negative findings. title: Bidirectional interplay of the gut microbiota and herbal medicine in Alzheimer's disease: mechanisms and therapeutic prospects.
abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder in which alterations in the gut microbiota and microbiota-gut-brain axis (MGBA) may contribute to disease-related pathological processes. Herbal medicines have long been used for memory impairment and age-related cognitive disorders and contain bioactive constituents with diverse molecular targets. title: Diet-microbiome interaction shapes stress susceptibility via a gut-brain neurometabolic circuit.
abstract: Dietary patterns shape mood and behavior, yet the microbial signals and neurosensory mechanisms underlying these effects remain unclear. Here, we identify a microbiota-mediated gut-brain circuit that dynamically regulates stress susceptibility during high-fat diet (HFD) exposure. title: Diet-Driven Modulation of the Gut Microbiome to Enhance Neuroplasticity and Cognitive Recovery After Ischemic Stroke.
abstract: Cognitive impairment and limited neuroplastic recovery remain major contributors to long-term disability following ischemic stroke. Increasing evidence suggests that stroke-induced disruption of the gut-brain axis, characterized by microbiome dysbiosis and altered microbial metabolite signaling, may influence post-stroke inflammation, synaptic remodeling, and cognitive outcomes. journal: Journal of the American Heart Association

title: Characterisation of Limosilactobacillus reuteri BG-R33®, an evolved aerotolerant derivative of the probiotic strain ATCC PTA 5289.
abstract: Probiotic strains intended for use in the oral cavity and upper respiratory tract are exposed to substantially higher oxygen levels than strains targeting the intestinal environment. We hypothesised that continuous oxygen exposure of an established probiotic strain used under conditions of high oxidative pressure, namely Limosilactobacillus reuteri ATCC PTA 5289 (Lr5289), would enable the natural selection of a variant better adapted to such an environment. title: Processing-controlled conjugation level of black tea polysaccharides regulates distinct microbial-metabolic pathways in intestinal protection.
abstract: Tea polysaccharides (TPS) usually conjugate with phenolics and proteins, but how conjugation levels affect their functionality is unclear. Here, black tea polysaccharides (BTPS) with graded conjugation levels were prepared by modulating enzymatic oxidation during rolling. Higher conjugation alters BTPS monosaccharide composition, particle size, surface charge, and morphology. title: Application of IgA-Seq in schizophrenia to identify key gut bacteria that promote abnormal behavior in mice.
abstract: Schizophrenia (SCZ) has a complex etiology, and growing evidence implicates the microbiota-gut-brain axis. Because abundance-based profiling does not identify taxa closely engaged by mucosal immunity, we used immunoglobulin A (IgA)-based bacterial sorting to prioritize candidate SCZ-associated gut bacteria and evaluated cultured consortia in mouse models. title: A putative model of the gut-muscle axis in aged livestock
abstract: The gut-muscle axis has been proposed to link gut microbiota with skeletal muscle physiology, yet its universality across livestock species remains unclear. Using aged laying hens, a livestock model with a relatively short digestive tract, we examined the gut microbiota, faecal metabolome, and breast-muscle metabolome by integrative multi-omics analyses in hens fed a Caldifermentibacillus hisashii-containing fermented feed or a control diet. title: Effects of succinate supplementation on rumen fermentation, microbiota, and propionate-associated metabolism in vitro
abstract: Introduction Succinate is an intermediate in the ruminal succinate-propionate pathway, but its direct effects as an exogenous additive on rumen fermentation, bacterial community structure, and energy-related metabolites remain insufficiently characterized. This study evaluated whether graded succinate supplementation changes in vitro rumen fermentation and propionate-associated microbial and metabolite profiles. title: Muribaculum intestinale restricts Salmonella Typhimurium colonization by converting succinate to propionate
abstract: Abstract Insufficient dietary fiber intake is associated with dysbiosis and compromised colonization resistance (CR) to enteric infections. However, a detailed understanding of the relationship between dietary fiber insufficiency and CR remains elusive. Our study aimed to delineate the impact of fiber deprivation on gut microbiome and CR in a murine model with Salmonella Typhimurium infection.
